sections.title: 1. Lab: Strands agent with custom tools

keyTerms.definition: The code-first open-source Python SDK for building agents.
The cycle: send the prompt to the model, run the tool, return the result, repeat until a final answer.
The decorator that turns a plain Python function into a callable tool.
Becomes the tool description. The model reads it to decide what to call.
The multi-agent orchestration framework used in chapter 3.

recall.question: What are the three parts of an agent?
recall.answer: A model, which is the brain. Tools, which are the hands. A prompt, which is the personality and instructions.

recall.question: Why does a vague docstring break tool selection?
recall.answer: The docstring is the routing logic the model reads. A docstring like utility function makes selection random.

recall.question: Five tool calls on a 2,000-token context: how many invocations do you pay for?
recall.answer: About five, not one. Each tool call costs another model invocation, and history grows each turn.

keyTerms.definition: Deterministic multi-step GenAI workflows defined as JSON with nodes and connections.
The version holding the latest changes after PrepareFlow, used for testing.
A named pointer to a numbered version. It keeps production on tested prompts.
Packages the latest flow changes into the DRAFT version for testing.
Moves a named output of one node to a named input of the next.

recall.question: When do you use a Flow instead of an agent?
recall.answer: When the path is fixed. A fixed three-step chain is a flow. A task where the model must decide which tools to call is an agent.

recall.question: What is the DRAFT, version, alias lifecycle?
recall.answer: After edits, run PrepareFlow to package changes into DRAFT for testing. A version is an immutable numbered snapshot. An alias like prod points at one version.

recall.question: What is the most common flow bug?
recall.answer: A targetInput name that does not match a placeholder in the prompt template. The step runs with an empty variable.

keyTerms.definition: The open-source multi-agent orchestration framework. The pip package is agent-squad.
The model call that reads the request and picks the specialist agent.
The chat history layer. In-memory by default, DynamoDB or SQL for production.
A composite agent running a fixed pipeline where each agent's output feeds the next.

recall.question: What does the classifier read, and what breaks routing?
recall.answer: It reads agent descriptions, not code or keywords. Overlapping descriptions make routing a coin flip.

recall.question: The three-specialist scenario: which two options are correct?
recall.answer: A: an Agent Squad orchestrator with a BedrockClassifier in front. C: DynamoDB-backed ChatStorage keyed by user ID and session ID.

recall.question: Why is in-memory ChatStorage wrong for production?
recall.answer: Every restart deletes conversation history, and multi-instance deployments do not agree. Use DynamoDB.

sections.title: 4. Lab: Lambda as Bedrock front end

keyTerms.definition: Holds the model identifier as runtime configuration. Switching models needs no redeploy.
The Lambda handler returns statusCode, headers, and a JSON-stringified body.
The API for streaming long token streams to browsers.
The managed front door: a stable HTTPS endpoint with authentication, throttling, and routing.

recall.question: What is the exam's model-switching trio?
recall.answer: Lambda holds the routing logic, API Gateway holds the stable endpoint, and AppConfig holds the model identifier as runtime configuration.

recall.question: Why not call Bedrock directly from a browser or mobile app?
recall.answer: It sends AWS credentials to the client and gives every client direct model access with no throttling.

recall.question: The mobile-app scenario: which three options are correct?
recall.answer: A: API Gateway with throttling and a Cognito authorizer. B: the model identifier in AppConfig, read at runtime. C: request logic in Lambda calling Bedrock with the Converse API.

keyTerms.definition: Connects the agent to a Lambda function plus a schema describing the functions.
Packages configuration changes into the DRAFT version. The agent ignores new groups until it runs.
The response field carrying the result: response.functionResponse.responseBody.TEXT.body.
The action-group style describing REST-style operations with apiPath and httpMethod.

recall.question: What is the single most common agent bug?
recall.answer: The DRAFT was never prepared, or the alias still points at the old version. The agent acts as if the new action group does not exist.

recall.question: The action runs but the agent reports a tool error. Most likely cause?
recall.answer: The Lambda returned a JSON object as the body instead of a string. The contract requires the result in responseBody.TEXT.body as a string.

recall.question: What are the two action-group schema styles?
recall.answer: Function details: simple named functions with parameters. OpenAPI schema: REST-style operations with apiPath and httpMethod.

keyTerms.definition: Serverless hosting for your agent container, with sessions, memory, and identity.
Turns existing APIs and Lambda functions into MCP-compatible tools.
Managed short-term and long-term agent context.
The fixed container route. The platform POSTs agent requests here.
The SDK wrapper implementing the container contract. Mark one function with app.entrypoint.

recall.question: What are the five parts of AgentCore?
recall.answer: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, and Observability.

recall.question: What is the fixed container contract?
recall.answer: Listen on port 8080. Answer POST /invocations with the agent logic. Answer GET /ping as a health check.

recall.question: Why is Lambda for agents wrong for long-running agent sessions?
recall.answer: Lambda caps executions at 15 minutes and has no session concept. Runtime manages long-lived sessions with health checks and idle timeouts.

sections.title: 7. Supporting labs: KMS, X-Ray, SQS, and foundations

keyTerms.definition: A data key encrypts the data locally. The KMS key encrypts the data key.
Traces requests across service boundaries and shows each segment's latency.
The managed message queue. It decouples ingestion from processing and buffers surges.
Instance Metadata Service version 2, the session-token-based metadata endpoint.
The service for ordered, replayable streams.

recall.question: The RAG ingestion practice question: which three options are correct?
recall.answer: A: buffer incoming documents with SQS. B: encrypt the S3 buckets with KMS customer-managed keys. C: enable X-Ray tracing across the ingestion Lambdas.

recall.question: Where did the 8 seconds go? Which service answers, and which does not?
recall.answer: X-Ray traces latency across calls. CloudTrail is audit logging, not performance tracing.

recall.question: What happens if you skip structure extraction?
recall.answer: Tables and headings break across chunks, retrieval quality drops, and RAG answers go bad. The exam hides this root cause in ingestion.

keyTerms.definition: The Cloud Development Kit. Define cloud infrastructure in TypeScript or Python, compiled to CloudFormation.
Compiles CDK code into a CloudFormation template.
Shows the change set. Review it before deploy, because a small change can replace a database.
Small building blocks like a Lambda function, an S3 bucket, or a DynamoDB table.

recall.question: What is the CDK workflow in four steps?
recall.answer: Write constructs in code, run cdk synth to build the template, run cdk diff and review it, then cdk deploy.

recall.question: Why is CDK the wrong answer for switch models without redeploy?
recall.answer: CDK is deploy-time infrastructure, not runtime configuration. AppConfig switches models at runtime.

recall.question: The dev, staging, prod scenario: which approach is correct?
recall.answer: B: one CDK stack class with one instance per environment, the Lambda role with bedrock:InvokeModel scoped to specific model ARNs, and cdk diff reviewed before each deploy.

keyTerms.definition: A build phase that runs an evaluation suite and fails the build on regression.
The file controlling the CodeBuild build: install, pre_build, build, and post_build phases.
The dataset the candidate is scored against in the gate.
The AWS service controlling the source, build, test, and deploy stages.

recall.question: The weekly prompt-edit scenario: which approach most reduces recurrence?
recall.answer: B: check prompts into git, run CodePipeline, and have CodeBuild execute an evaluation gate on a golden dataset with toxicity and refusal thresholds. Failures block deployment.

recall.question: What is an evaluation gate NOT?
recall.answer: Not run the model once and look at it. It is a repeatable suite with thresholds, checked into the repository, running on every change.

recall.question: What breaks if the golden dataset is old?
recall.answer: The gate tests yesterday's product. Refresh it from production traffic.
